website.readmeExcerpt:
# Macrology

**This plugin is still under heavy development and is not
stable. Proceed with caution.**

## Description

This command allows you to create better and unrestricted macros.

Unlike normal macros, you can't assign them to hotbar buttons (yet?), but you can
execute them using commands (and custom commands), run multiple at the
same time, pause them, make them loop, use `<wait.X>` with fractional
seconds, and, of course, make them as long as you please (the *macro*
part of macro macros).

Lastly, you can also organise macros into folders (and nest folders)
for easier access.

## Install

- Add `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GiR-Zippo/Macrology/main/data/pluginmaster.json` to your list of custom repositories.
- Install via `/xlplugins`.

## Commands

- `/mmacros` - opens the main interface
- `/mmacro <uuid>` - executes the macro with the given UUID
- `/mmcancel <all|uuid>` - either cancels all currently-running macros
  or cancels the first instance of the macro represented by the given
  UUID

## Special macro properties

### Looping

Macro macros can loop by using the `/loop` command. Whenever this
command is encountered in a macro, it will start the macro over from
the beginning.

### Pausing

In the main interface, there is a list of currently-running macros. If
you click on one and click "Pause" below, it will pause the
macro. Clicking "Resume" after will resume it from where it left off.

### Parallel macros

You can run more than one macro macro at the same time. This is an
inherent feature and you don't have to do anything to enable it. Just
run two or more macros, and they'll run in parallel.

### Fractional `<wait.#>`

When using `<wait.#>` in a macro, you can use decimal points, like
`<wait.2.5>`.

## Known issues

- There is no way good way to reorder macros.
- There is no way to take a macro out of a folder (i.e. put it back at the root).

plugins.name: Mahjong Advisor
plugins.punchline: Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.
plugins.description:
Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.

plugins.changelog: v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.

The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.

website.title: MahjongAdvisor
website.description: Doman Mahjong discard advisor for Dalamud. Reads your hand and ranks discards by hand speed vs deal-in risk.
website.readmeExcerpt:
# Mahjong Advisor

A Doman Mahjong discard advisor for Dalamud, by **Akari**. It reads your hand,
the discards, the dora, the scores and the called melds, then ranks each legal
discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by
default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays. Manual suggestion
mode is one command away (`/mjadv stop`).

**0.4.0.0** is the current public build. The engine and most of the reader were
played live before this version; the meld mapping, the call-prompt fixes, the
expected-value model and the new auto-play controller still need a live pass.

## Projects

| Project | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Mahjong.Advisor` | Pure engine — shanten, ukeire, safety, threat model, discard and call ranking. No Dalamud reference. |
| `Mahjong.Advisor.Tests` | 193 xUnit tests over the engine, including the shanten vectors. |
| `Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin` | Dalamud shell — addon reading, overlay, control panel, JSONL game log, optional auto-play actuator. |
| `Mahjong.Advisor.Simulator` | Offline console app for tuning parameters against identical deals. |

The engine stays on `net8.0` so it loads under whatever runtime the host
provides. The plugin uses `Dalamud.NET.Sdk/15.0.0`, which resolves to
`net10.0-windows` at API level 15. The tests and simulator target `net9.0`, so a
local build needs both the .NET 9 and .NET 10 runtimes.

Clean-room implementation. Nothing is derived from the AGPL solver source; the
addon offsets and node ids are observable facts about the game client.

## Build and test

```powershell
dotnet test Mahjong.Advisor.Tests/Mahjong.Advisor.Tests.csproj -c Release
dotnet build Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin/Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin.csproj -c Release
```

The Release build runs DalamudPackager and produces
`Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin/bin/Release/Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin/latest.zip`.

Simulator sweeps:

```powershell
dotnet run --project Mahjong.Advisor.Simulator -c Release -- 200
```

200 hands is a smell test; 1000 is the smallest run whose differences are worth
acting on.

## First run

Open a Doman Mahjong table. The overlay appears by itself; there is no mapping
step.

- Discard piles are found automatically from their tile counts and positions.
  Memory reading takes over once enough tiles are down.
- Called-meld strips use the known node families (`112`-`115`). A mapping is
  only accepted when our own meld count agrees with the hand shape, so a wrong
  id degrades to "meld count unknown" instead of silently reading zero melds.
- If detection fails on your client, `/mjadv nodes` opens the control panel with
  the manual override and the node-tree dump. `/mjadv melds` prints the per-seat
  meld readout to the Dalamud log (`/xllog`).

Riichi is read from the marker node beside each pond. The rotation flag and the
score-drop heuristic are dead ends on this client and are no longer used to
declare riichi.

Auto-play and file logging are **on by default** in this build. `/mjadv stop`
turns auto-play off immediately and leaves the overlay as suggestions only;
`/mjadv auto on` turns it back on. Manual play and auto-play use the same reader
and advisor, so the overlay still shows the pick either way.

## UI

The **overlay** is the compact in-game window: current recommendation, the hand
in display order with the suggested tile bracketed, danger, alternatives and the
auto-play state.

The **control panel** is the installer's Open/Settings window. It has five tabs:

| Tab | Contents |
|---|---|
| Advisor | table state, recommendation, opponents, observation flags and read diagnostics |
| Automation | auto-play master switch, pon/chi/kan policy, result advancement and timing |
| Setup | pond/meld/hand-slot detection, manual override, node-tree and tile dumps |
| Settings | overlay visibility, logging and advisor tuning |
| About | build, author, commands and data sources |

The installer's **Open** button opens the control panel *and* the overlay;
**Settings** opens the control panel directly on the Settings tab.

## Auto-play (casual tables only)

The simplest way to run a test is:

```text
/mjadv session     # auto-play on, logging on, fresh log file
<play 2-3 casual hanchan>
/mjadv bundle      # zip of logs + config + layouts + last state
```

`/mjadv session` is also a button in the Automation tab. `/mjadv bundle` opens
the folder containing the zip when it finishes.

Auto-play replays the client's own FireCallback protocol:

- discard: `[15, iconId]` then `[7, slot]`
- call / self-action: `[11, option]`
- result screens: `[14]` at the agari modal, `[17]` at the end-of-hand transition

It deliberately **does not** advance the new-hand screen. The game fires that
acknowledgement itself; sending a second one desynced live tables in the
reference implementation.

The state machine also handles the NPC-table quirks observed in the first two
logged games:

- **State 15** is also the generic “other players are acting” state. It is only
  treated as a call prompt when real call buttons are readable; otherwise the
  overlay says “Waiting for other players” instead of showing stale advice.
- **State 22** is the forced discard after declaring riichi. The bot cuts the
  drawn tile immediately instead of waiting for the game’s timeout.
- **State 27** is the between-hands result/score screen. The game advances this
  itself, so the bot waits and shows “Result screen” rather than firing an
  unverified opcode.
- **Late-wall defence.** When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is
  down to the last four go-arounds, any hand that is not tenpai folds. Pushing
  a 1-shanten no-riichi hand there dealt 12,000 in a live game.
- **Silent-endgame floor.** The measured damaten curve topped out at 19%, so a
  table with no riichi and no melds read as harmless all the way to the end —
  live tiles got pushed one-away at wall 20 into silent tenpai twice in one
  match. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor rising from zero at wall
  32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, which arms the late-wall fold and per-
  tile safety ranking even when nobody shows a signal. A tile that is already
  in every opponent's pond outranks live efficiency in that endgame.
- A **self-kan bar** (`Kan / Pass` at state 6) is ignored. The client does not
  accept the Pass callback there; the bot just discards normally, which
  declines the kan. Firing Pass four times was the freeze in the first
  0.3.3.0 run.
- A **complete open hand with no yaku is not a win.** The bot checks for a yaku
  before firing the unlabelled tsumo option; otherwise it keeps discarding.
  Treating “complete” as “can win” was the second freeze.
- Call prompts now prefer the **newest board addition** over a stale pond tile.
  The second live log claimed a 6z dragon Pon while the actual claim was 9m,
  which opened a no-yaku hand. The log now records the pond’s last discard and
  seat so this is visible next time.
- Discard advice is only computed at our actual decision states (6/30/28/22), so
  a call or result screen can no longer leave an old “discard X” on the overlay.

Defaults are conservative:

- **Pon**: taken when the advisor says it is worth opening the hand.
- **Ron / tsumo**: always taken.
- **Riichi**: declared when the advisor says it is the best line.
- **Chi**: automated for single-shape calls. The controller calls chi when the
  advisor ranks it best and exactly one run shape is possible — that path
  completes with no dialog. When two or three shapes are possible the client
  opens its shape-selection surface, which ignores scripted call picks (the
  first picker dump proves it), so the controller passes instead and logs how
  many shapes it declined. The picker layout is still dumped once per session
  so shape-specific selection can be built later.
- **Kan**: off. A kan flips another dora indicator for every seat.
- A self-kan prompt that the advisor declines is answered by discarding, which
  the client accepts; firing the Pass callback there does nothing.
- Nine-terminals/honours is aborted unless the hand is a real kokushi attempt
  (thirteen-orphans shanten 2 or better).

The controller waits six seconds after a table appears before sending anything,
waits for a full readable hand, uses humanized think times, and retries a popup
fire up to four times if the prompt animation swallowed it. `/mjadv auto off` or
`/mjadv stop` is the panic switch.

Two extra guards protect the discard path:

- The display-slot tiles must exactly match the hand array before a discard is
  sent. A stale/shifted node id fails closed rather than cutting a tile you do
  not hold.
- After declaring riichi, the follow-up discard is chosen from the tenpai-keeping
  options and is not sent until the Riichi/Pass prompt has closed. The generic
  recommendation is never used for that cut.

## Tuning

The advisor is set to the fitted win-rate values:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Base hand value | 1300 |
| Caution (deal-in cost) | 5200 |
| Tenpai-at-draw value | 1500 |
| Opponent hand value | 4000 |

A one-time v3 config migration resets old custom values to these. After that,
changes made in Settings persist normally. `Reset to recommended` in Settings
restores the same values.

### Hand value

Completed hands are scored exactly — yaku, fu, dora, aka dora and the payment
table, from pinfu and yakuhai through honitsu, ittsuu and the yakuman. The
offline simulator uses that scoring for every win, including legality and
payouts. Live push/fold decisions still use the fitted dora model: a 1,500-hand
A/B of exact ready-hand valuation showed the two value scales must be unified
before they can be mixed (win rate fell from 15.4% to 8.1% because a ready hand
priced at its true 1,000-2,000 points lost to a one-away hand still carrying the
old ~3,000-point estimate). The exact valuation is implemented and unit-tested;
it stays out of the live decision until the scale is recalibrated for every
shanten.

## Commands

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `/mjadv` / `/mjadv show` | Show the overlay and reset its position |
| `/mjadv hide` / `/mjadv toggle` | Hide or toggle the overlay |
| `/mjadv setup` / `/mjadv config` | Open the control panel |
| `/mjadv session` | Auto-play + logging on, start a fresh log file |
| `/mjadv bundle` | Zip the recent logs, config, layouts and last state |
| `/mjadv folder` | Open the logs/diagnostics folder |
| `/mjadv auto` / `/mjadv auto [on/off]` | Toggle or set auto-play |
| `/mjadv stop` | Turn auto-play off |
| `/mjadv nodes` | Open the control panel on the node-mapping tab |
| `/mjadv melds` | Log each seat's meld count and tiles, plus the configured node families |
| `/mjadv hand` | Log the display-slot order, tile and icon id of every visible hand tile |
| `/mjadv options` | Log the current popup buttons and their `[11, n]` indices |
| `/mjadv log` | Toggle the JSONL decision log |
| `/mjadv geometry` | Dump tile geometry to a TSV file |
| `/mjadv snap` | Dump every visible node id to a TSV file (for snapshot diffing) |

## What is verified, and what is not

**Verified in game**

- Own hand, discards, dora, scores and wall count.
- Opponent riichi markers on all four seats.
- Self-riichi lock.
- Kuikae-forbidden discards after a call.
- Discard advice on every turn.
- The automatic pond mapping, including its self-correction when a pile goes
  lopsided.

**Fixed, but not yet played in this build**

- The meld container mapping and the readiness prior that uses it.
- Ron / tsumo / self-kan prompt handling.
- The expected-value discard model and the push horizon of 2.
- Opening the control panel only when asked.
- The auto-play controller: discard handshake, option indices, popup retries,
  result advancement and riichi follow-up. The protocol is taken from the
  reference solver's live captures, but this integration has not been played.

**Known limits**

- Meld mapping is a best-effort default. If it is rejected, readiness falls back
  to a quiet-hand floor plus part of the one-call rate; the overlay says so.
- Seat and round winds are still not read, so yakuhai detection is deliberately
  pessimistic.
- Alt-character retainers are irrelevant here, but the same principle applies to
  any "my own" detection: the client hides information.
- The simulator runs about 17% win / 10% deal-in / 12% draw against real play's
  roughly 21% / 13% / 16%. Use it to rank settings against each other, never to
  judge whether the advisor is good.

## Testing auto-play

Use a **casual** Doman Mahjong table, not a ranked/PvP mode. Suggested first
session:

1. Run `/mjadv session` (or click **Start auto-play session** in the Automation
   tab).
2. Play one hand and watch the first discard. If the wrong tile leaves, run
   `/mjadv stop` immediately.
3. Play 2–3 full hanchan (about 8–12 hands).
4. Run `/mjadv bundle` and send the zip it opens. It contains the JSONL logs,
   config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot.
5. Toggle `/mjadv stop` and confirm manual play returns to suggestion-only.

The controller logs every sent input under `[MahjongAdvisor][auto]` in
`/xllog`, writes `Kind: "auto"` records for sent inputs, and writes
`Kind: "auto-status"` records whenever its status changes (waiting, settling,
stalled, hand-slot mismatch, and so on). That status trail is the main thing
that makes a failed run diagnosable.

## Diagnostics

Every decision can be written as one JSONL record. Logging is on by default;
records land in `%APPDATA%\XIVLauncher\pluginConfigs\Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin\logs\`.

Each record carries the build stamp, full table state, observation flags, every
candidate's score, the meld readout, the raw call-prompt values and the nodes
that became visible that tick. Auto-play adds `Kind: "auto"` action records and
`Kind: "auto-status"` records whenever it starts waiting, settles, stalls or
refuses a discard.

`/mjadv bundle` zips the recent logs, config, layouts, the last 5,000 lines of
`dalamud.log` and a full last-read snapshot into
`...\pluginConfigs\Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin\diagnostics\`. The bundle can contain
player names from the log, so review it before sharing.

## Data sources

Win rates and opponent readiness come from `HououTables`, measured across about
1.2 million games in Tenhou's top lobby
(`chienshyong/houou-statistics`, forked from `Euophrys/houou-analysis`).

## Release

Bump all four places together:

1. `Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin/Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin.csproj` — `<Version>`
2. `Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin/Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin.json` — `AssemblyVersion` and `TestingAssemblyVersion`
3. `repo.json` — `AssemblyVersion`, `TestingAssemblyVersion`, `Changelog` and the download links
4. `Logging/GameLogger.cs` — `BuildStamp`

Then:

```powershell
git add .
git commit -m "Mahjong Advisor v0.4.0.0"
git push origin main
git tag v0.4.0.0
git push origin v0.4.0.0
```

CI runs the tests, builds the plugin and publishes `MahjongAdvisor.zip` on the
GitHub Release. After the release exists, add the repo to the combined
pluginmaster (`DalamudPlugins/Build-CombinedRepo.ps1`) and push it.

The version-bump rule is absolute: a tag that has been pushed is spent and must
never be reused, including when the only change is a failed build.

website.readmeExcerpt:
# Auto Mahjong Solver

A Dalamud plugin that reads FFXIV Doman Mahjong, computes the mathematically best discard and call, shows a suggestion overlay, and (optionally, behind a gate) plays for you.

Command: `/amjs` (alias `/mahjong`).

## Status

The solver engine, board reading, and the autonomous play loop are live-verified on casual tables
(multi-hand sessions without stalls). Riichi declaration and the defense layer are implemented and
await their first observed in-game trigger.

| Capability | State |
|---|---|
| Solver engine (shanten, ukeire) | Implemented, unit-tested |
| Yaku / Doman scoring | Implemented, unit-tested; han→points table pending live verification |
| `Emj` hand reader (closed hand, aka) | **Verified live** (incl. under popups) |
| `Emj` meld reader (chii/pon/kan, feeds meldCount) | **Verified live** — meld strips mapped (self=112 family); post-call discard state 28 handled |
| `Emj` addon reader (rivers, dora, winds, scores, riichi badges) | Implemented; opponent river↔panel pairing pending live verification (`/amjs state`) |
| Seen-tile ukeire + furiten avoidance + fold vs riichi | Implemented; fold path awaits first observed opponent riichi |
| Auto-riichi (declare on live closed tenpai, then tsumogiri) | **Verified live** |
| Auto-play loop (discard, win, calls, redeal prompt, result screens) | **Verified live** — multi-hand sessions; popup fires retry-verified; settle grace + stall watchdog |
| Nine-terminals redeal prompt (keep on kokushi shanten ≤ 2) | Implemented; option label match pending first observation |
| Value-aware discard EV (exact points EV at tenpai; dora/aka/yakuhai retention above) | Implemented, unit-tested |
| Shared turn policy (engine `TurnPolicy`, used by bot and simulator) | Implemented |
| Self-play simulator (`tools/AutoMahjongSolver.Simulator`) | Implemented; baseline below |
| Calling strategy v1 (pon: yakuhai / secured-yaku / dora-tanyao; chi+kan never) | Implemented, unit-tested, simulated; pending live verification |
| Suggestion overlay | Planned |
| Chi / kan calls | Planned (chi variant-selection UI unverified; kan flips unreadable dora) |

## Layout

- `AutoMahjongSolver.Engine` — pure C# (`net10.0`), no Dalamud dependency. Tiles, shanten, ukeire, and (later) yaku/scoring. Fully unit-testable offline.
- `tests/AutoMahjongSolver.Engine.Tests` — xUnit tests for the engine.
- `AutoMahjongSolver` — the Dalamud plugin (planned): `Emj` reader, suggestion overlay, gated actuation. Built on ECommons.

## Build

```
dotnet test                                                   # engine + tests (no game required)
dotnet run --project tools/AutoMahjongSolver.Simulator -c Release -- 200 7   # self-play: matches, seed
```

Self-play baseline (200 matches, seed 7, all four seats on the current policy), with pon calls
(2026-06-12): 1125 hands, ~17.5% win rate per seat-hand, ~9.7% deal-in, ~30.5% riichi, 30.1%
exhaustive draws, average win 5990 points / 3.31 han. The closed-hands-only run before calls was
38.7% draws / 15.3% wins / 7.2% deal-in / avg win 7302 — pon trades win size for completion rate.
Policy changes should be judged against these numbers, same seed.

The Dalamud plugin project builds against `Dalamud.NET.Sdk` and requires a Dalamud dev environment.

## Notes

Doman Mahjong is standard 4-player Japanese riichi with FFXIV-specific scoring: a flat han-to-points table with **no fu calculation**. The engine targets this ruleset.

Auto-play of a ranked, human-PvP minigame carries account risk. Auto-play is off by default, gated behind an explicit opt-in, and disabled in ranked rooms.

# Mannerisms

**Your character has a personality now.**

Mannerisms is a Dalamud plugin that brings your FFXIV character to life. Set up gestures that suggest emotes based on what you type in chat: type "bye" and get a wave suggestion, say "WHAT" and see the aback emote ready to fire. One click or keybind to accept.

## Features

### Gesture Suggestions

Mannerisms watches what you type in chat and suggests matching emotes in a floating picker window. You stay in control: suggestions appear, you decide whether to use them.

- **Three trigger modes**: Common (pre-made toggleable patterns), Simple (build patterns with a comma-separated word list), and Advanced (full regex)
- **Per-character profiles** with independent gesture sets
- **Target-aware triggers** that only fire when you have a target, or when your target matches the recipient of a tell
- **Party-aware triggers** that verify your target is in your party
- **Configurable keybinds** to accept or dismiss suggestions without touching the mouse
- **Suggestion timeout** with visual countdown: suggestions fade if you don't act on them

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `/manners` | Open the configuration window |

## Installation

Mannerisms is available in the Dalamud Plugin Installer. Open `/xlplugins` and search for **Mannerisms**.

## Support

If you enjoy Mannerisms, consider supporting development:

[![Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ko--fi-Support-ff5e5b?logo=ko-fi)](https://ko-fi.teejaylabs.com/)

plugins.description:
Market Helper is an all-in-one market board tool with five tabs:

UNDERCUT — Walk a summoning bell's retainers and undercut every listed item. HQ and NQ are handled separately, your own retainers are matched rather than undercut, per-item overrides and price memory are supported, an obvious troll price is skipped, and mannequin/display items are never touched (if a row can't be verified it is skipped rather than risk delisting it). Closes the bell when it finishes.

LISTER — Build a list (hold CTRL and hover an item, or search) and press Go to list them all. Prices each item at the most common market price, ignoring lone troll listings, against your world, data center or whole region. Per-item stack sizes and list amounts, rolls extra items to the next retainer at the 20-slot cap, and includes a no-touch dry run.

FLIPPER — Compare any marketable item across Japan, America, Europe and Materia via Universalis. Top 10 listings per region, best cross-region flip, and seller/buyer tax modelling.

ITEM GATHERER — Pull designated items off your retainers into your bags, optionally returning your market listings first. Manual withdraw/deposit actions included.

BUYER — Build a shopping list by hand or import a MakePlace furniture list, then SCAN the market per world via Universalis and press SEND to travel with Lifestream and buy across worlds. Every purchase is verified against the game's own confirmation dialog before it is accepted. Listings are bought whole, so by default it never buys a bigger stack than you still need, and a hard sanity ceiling caps the price even with no cap set. If a planned listing has already been bought it chases the next cheapest, on other worlds if needed, until your order is filled. Dry run is on by default.

Open with /markethelp, /market, /mh, or /undercut.
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json

website.title: MarketHelper
website.readmeExcerpt:
# Market Helper

An all-in-one FFXIV market board plugin for [Dalamud](https://github.com/goatcorp/Dalamud).

Open with `/markethelp`, `/market`, `/mh`, or `/undercut`.

## Features

### Undercut
Stand near a summoning bell and press **Run**. Market Helper walks every retainer on the bell and undercuts each listed item to the lowest price.
- HQ/NQ handling and own-retainer protection
- Per-item price overrides and price memory within a run
- Skips mannequin / display items (detected by the game's mannequin icon) so they're never touched or delisted

### Lister
Build a list of items — hold **CTRL** and hover an item to quick-add it, or search by name. Press **Go** and it walks the bell and lists them all.
- Prices each item at the most common market price (ignoring lone troll/outlier listings), minus your undercut
- Price against your world, data center, or whole region (via Universalis)
- Handles the 20-item-per-retainer cap by rolling extra items to the next retainer
- No-touch **dry run** previews exactly what it would list, and at what price, before touching the market

### Flipper
Search any marketable item and compare prices across Japan, America, Europe and Materia via [Universalis](https://universalis.app).
- Top 10 listings per region
- Best cross-region flip (cheapest buy vs dearest sell)
- Seller/buyer tax modeling

## Installation

Add this URL to Dalamud's custom plugin repositories (`/xlsettings` → Experimental → Custom Plugin Repositories):

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json
```

Then find **Market Helper** in the plugin installer.

## Credits
Author: Akari (dexcss). Built on [ECommons](https://github.com/NightmareXIV/ECommons). Market data from [Universalis](https://universalis.app).

## Disclaimer
Automating retainer and market board actions may carry risk. Use at your own discretion. Always run the Lister's **dry run** first to confirm items and prices before listing for real.

website.readmeExcerpt:
﻿# MaskedCarnivale **MaskedCarnivale** allows you to record, or stream your game without displaying Dalamud plugins. The plugin creates a second window in the background which can be recorded using software like OBS. Optionally you can also have the window display the game without a UI at all, so you can take immersive recordings. The plugin menu can be displayed by typing /carnivale in chat or by using /carnivale enable or /carnivale disable to start or stop the window. ## Testing exclusive This plugin is testing exclusive. You must enable plugin testing before you can install it. To do so, follow this set of instructions: 1. Go to `/xlsettings` 2. Go to "Experimental" tab 3. Enable "Get plugins testing builds" checkbox 4. Save settings by pressing a :floppy_disk: button in bottom right corner of the window Now you can proceed to install the plugin. ## Known issues Gamma should be set to any value other than 50 for mode with UI to work. **Please note**: This plugin only hides overlay plugins, plugins which actually modify the contents of the game still will be visible. For example the dalamud menu itself would be hidden but the dalamud button on the escape menu would still show up and thus it is advised to disable it in the dalamud settings. Plugins such as penumbra, cammy, and the tweaks allowing you to change the layout of the castbar would still be visible. To display a mouse cursor enable software cursor ingame, though most streamers currently dont show their cursor anyway. To move the window use the XY offset in the plugin menu. The UI can be hidden in the plugin menu. The plugin menu can be displayed by typing /carnivale in chat. Have fun streaming the game without suffering bad QoL and horrid latency! 4: Click on the Save icon button at the bottom right side of the window. The plugins should now be available under All Plugins in the Plugins Installer window, accessable via the button/menu or typing /xlplugins. ## This plugin is in development This means that there are still features that I would like to implement in future or features that I would like to enhance, as well as that I'm accepting suggestions and feature requests. ## Installation 1. Install [FFXIVQuickLauncher](https://github.com/goatcorp/FFXIVQuickLauncher?tab=readme-ov-file#xivlauncher-----) and enable Dalamud in it's settings. You have to run the game through FFXIVQuickLauncher in order for any of these plugins to work. 2. Open Dalamud settings by typing `/xlsettings` in game chat. 3. Go to "Experimental" tab. 4. Find "Custom Plugin Repositories" section, agree with listed terms if needed and paste the following link into text input field: `https://github.com/NightmareXIV/MyDalamudPlugins/raw/main/pluginmaster.json` 5. Click "Save" button. You should now have NightmareXIV plugins available in your plugin installer.
Open plugin installer by typing `/xlplugins` in game chat, go to "Available plugins" section and search for a plugin you would like to install. ![image](https://github.com/NightmareXIV/MyDalamudPlugins/blob/main/meta/install/installer.png?raw=true) ## Support Join NightmareXIV Discord server to receive support for this plugin: https://discord.gg/m8NRt4X8Gf [![](https://dcbadge.vercel.app/api/server/m8NRt4X8Gf)](https://discord.gg/m8NRt4X8Gf) The server operates on a ticket-based system. Please create a ticket and describe your issue. Additionally, you may create an issue in the repository. Reply time for tickets may be significantly longer than on Discord, however, the issue does not have any risks to be lost. (Basically, if you want to report a critical bug or receive help, prefer Discord, if you want to suggest feature or report non-critical bug, prefer Github)

website.title: mask-of-kefka
website.description: Streamer mode for FFXIV: stream the game without showing Dalamud plugin overlays
website.readmeExcerpt: # Mask of Kefka A [Dalamud](https://dalamud.dev) plugin for FFXIV that creates a **second window with a clean image of the game**: no ImGui, no plugin overlays, no Dalamud at all. Capture that window in OBS and stream with all your quality-of-life plugins without showing them. In short: a **streamer mode** (stream mode) for FFXIV. Inspired by [MaskedCarnivale (ProjectMimer)](https://github.com/ProjectMimer/MaskedCarnivale), rewritten from scratch for current Dalamud. ## Disclaimer **This plugin was not made to deceive anyone. It was made to protect your account. Use it responsibly.** Square Enix prohibits all third-party tools. Showing them on stream creates a permanent, public record that can be acted upon. This plugin exists so that streamers who already use quality-of-life plugins do not expose themselves on video. It does not make using third-party tools allowed, it does not hide them from Square Enix, and it does not reduce any risk other than the visual one. What you do with your account remains your responsibility. ## Features - Clean mirror of the game (scene + game UI) in a separate window, free of any Dalamud overlay. - Optional no-UI mode: shows only the scene, for immersive recordings. - Borderless mode: hides the title bar for a clean capture. Drag the window from anywhere inside it and resize from the edges. - Output rate limiter: render 1 frame every N to cut the GPU cost of the output. ## What it does NOT hide (read this before streaming) The plugin hides **ImGui overlays only**: Dalamud windows, plugin windows, and anything else drawn on top of the game by Dalamud. Everything that is part of the game itself stays visible, including changes made by plugins: - **Plugins that modify the game content** (Penumbra, Glamourer, Mare and similar): model, texture and animation changes are part of the rendered scene and show up in the output. - **Plugins that write to the game chat**: chat is game UI. Any plugin message printed there appears on stream. - **Plugins that modify native game UI** (nameplates, cast bars, party list tweaks and similar): they edit the game's own elements, which the output shows. - **The Dalamud entry in the game's system menu**: drawn by the game UI. Disable it in the Dalamud settings if needed. Before going live, open the output window and check what your specific plugin set looks like in it. When in doubt, assume that anything you can see without opening a floating window will be visible on stream. ## Commands | Command | Effect | |---|---| | `/kefka` | Opens the configuration window | | `/kefka on` / `/kefka off` | Starts/stops the output window | | `/kefka ui` | Toggles the game UI in the output | ## Capturing in OBS 1. Enable the output window (`/kefka on`). 2. In OBS, add a **Window Capture** source and select the `Mask of Kefka` window. 3. Use the **Windows 10 (1903 and up)** capture method (Windows Graphics Capture). 4. **Minimize the Mask of Kefka window** once the capture is set up (there is a button for it in `/kefka`). Step 4 matters: while the output window is visible, Windows composes it every frame and the game can lose a significant amount of fps (the game window may also drop out of its optimized fullscreen presentation). Minimized, the cost is virtually zero. On current Windows 11 the capture keeps updating normally while the window is minimized; if your capture freezes instead (older Windows builds), keep the window visible but small and consider the output rate limiter in `/kefka`. Do not use Game Capture: it hooks the game process and captures the main window, overlays included. The same applies to Discord screen sharing and similar tools: share the `Mask of Kefka` window, not the game, and minimize it after picking it (do a quick test on your setup first). Tips: - To show your cursor on stream, enable the software cursor in the game settings. The hardware cursor does not appear in the capture. - Enable the borderless option in `/kefka` so the title bar does not show up in the capture. ## Installing Requirements: [XIVLauncher](https://goatcorp.github.io/) with Dalamud enabled. 1. In game, type `/xlsettings` and open the **Experimental** tab. 2. Under **Custom Plugin Repositories**, paste the URL below into an empty box: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/doomzao/plugins/main/repo.json ``` 3. Click the **+** button on the right, then the **save** button at the bottom right. 4. Open `/xlplugins`, search for **Mask of Kefka** (or "streamer mode") and install it. That repository URL covers all my plugins: add it once and future plugins appear in the installer automatically. ### Building from source Requires the [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0). ```powershell dotnet build -c Release ``` Then, in game: 1. `/xlsettings`, then the **Experimental** tab, then **Dev Plugin Locations**. 2. Add the path `...\mask-of-kefka\MaskOfKefka\bin\Release\MaskOfKefka.dll` and save. 3. `/xlplugins`, then **Dev Tools**, then **Installed Dev Plugins**, and enable Mask of Kefka. ## Known limitations and possible failures - **HDR**: the output window is SDR. With the game in HDR the colors may look washed out; prefer SDR for streaming. - **The no-UI mode breaks on game patches.** It depends on a render target index that shifts whenever Square Enix touches the graphics pipeline. It is reconfigurable in the plugin settings without a rebuild, and while the index is invalid the output safely falls back to the with-UI mode. The default with-UI mode does not use any index and keeps working across patches. - **Game or Dalamud updates can break the plugin entirely** (it stops loading or compiling) until it is updated. This is true for every Dalamud plugin. - **Hardware cursor is not captured.** Enable the software cursor in the game settings if you want the cursor on stream. - **Audio is not part of the window.** Capture the game audio in OBS as usual (desktop or application audio); the output window only carries video. - **A visible output window can cost game fps.** Minimize it while streaming (see Capturing in OBS). On older Windows builds the capture may freeze while minimized; in that case keep the window small and visible instead. - **OBS Game Capture does not work for this**; it hooks the game and captures the main window, overlays included. Use Window Capture on the output window. - **Failure behavior**: if rendering fails repeatedly (for example after a video device reset), the plugin logs the error and shuts the output down instead of crashing the game. Reopen it with `/kefka on`. - This plugin is young and has not been battle-tested across every setup (multi-monitor DPI mixes, HDR, exotic drivers). If something looks wrong, open an issue with your setup details. ## License [AGPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE)

Repo URL ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PassiveModding/Meddle/main/repo.json ``` ## Attributions Much of this code is from or based on the following projects and wouldn't have been possible without them: - [Xande](https://github.com/xivdev/Xande) [[GNU AGPL v3](https://github.com/xivdev/Xande/blob/main/LICENSE)] - PBD file structure - MeshBuilder - RaceDeformer - Havok Skeletons - [Penumbra](https://github.com/xivdev/Penumbra) - shader comp logic - vertex type info - SpanBinaryReader - [Lumina](https://github.com/NotAdam/Lumina/) - file structures - [SaintCoinach](https://github.com/xivapi/SaintCoinach) - terrain and level file structures - [Alpha](https://github.com/NotNite/Alpha) [[MIT](https://github.com/NotNite/Alpha/blob/main/LICENSE)] - initial reference for Meddle.UI project setup and draw logic - [PathFinder](https://github.com/chirpxiv/ffxiv-pathfinder) [[MIT](https://github.com/chirpxiv/ffxiv-pathfinder/blob/main/LICENSE)] - 🐇 - reference for world overlay logic - [Ktisis](https://github.com/ktisis-tools/Ktisis) [[GNU GPL v3](https://github.com/ktisis-tools/Ktisis/blob/main/LICENSE)] - lighting structs - hkQsTransformf matrix handling Important contributors: - [WorkingRobot](https://github.com/WorkingRobot) - GPU texture exports - Character-tree structure for exports - Shape and attribute data - Attach structs - Skeleton Parsing - Members of the Penumbra discord - Testing and feedback
