website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto Hunt Train

Hunt trains, ridden for you. Built on Dalamud.

--- ## What it does Hears a hunt train being called anywhere in your region, gets your character to the start aetheryte on that world, follows the conductor's flags from mark to mark, and lands a hit on every A rank before the crowd deletes it. ## Features - **Rides announced trains**: HuntAlerts detects the trains; this plugin lists them from every region under a view you pick (My data centers, My region or Everywhere), each with a countdown, a region tag when it runs outside yours, and a Ride button that takes any train in your region, on any data center, and says why it is off when it cannot. - **Train details**: click a train for its start time and countdown, start zone, aetheryte, conductor, post time and the full announcement cleaned for reading, with buttons to ride it, flag its start on the map, open the Party Finder on Hunts, point an on-screen arrow at the start, or relay a one-line summary (with ``) to any chat channel. - **Train notifications**: a chat line with a link to the train's details and an optional game sound, and, for a train you could ride on your allowed data centers, the Train page opening by itself and the taskbar flashing while the game is in the background. Switch HuntAlerts' own chat alert and banner off to avoid doubles. - **Auto-join**: off by default; switch it on per expansion to have trains joined without a click, limited to your allowed data centers, with or without data center transfers, and with the lead time a train on another data center needs before auto-join commits. A GM alert switches it off. - **Gets you there**: world change, data center travel and instance switching through Lifestream, then the plugin's own teleport and flight to the start aetheryte. - **Follows the conductor**: reads the conductor's map flags from Shout, Yell and Say, picks the nearest aetheryte or flies when the flag is close, and understands instance numbers. - **Finds the conductor**: from the announcement when it names one, from the first flag posted in the start zone, or picked by hand. - **Catches up with a train in progress**: a train more than three minutes past its start has left its start zone, so the ride estimates how far along its expansion's usual route the train has got, teleports there and listens for the next flag, moving on a zone at a time until it hears one. - **Hits, never leads**: dismounts at range, waits for the conductor's pull, lands a hit on the zone's A rank for credit, and never starts a pull or drags adds into the crowd. - **Knows when it's over**: ends the ride once every A rank of the expansion is credited, or when the conductor has gone quiet. - **Way home**: return to your home world after the train, stay for the next one, or run the after-ride action. - **Recovery**: gets back up after a death and rejoins the train; re-paths, jumps, or teleports out when it gets stuck. - **Auto-repair**: Dark Matter during a lull between flags; the Grand Company mender only before a data center transfer. - **Auto-consume**: keeps food and medicine buffs up in the lulls between flags, HQ first. - **Pause & resume**: park a ride without losing your progress, auto-pause while you're in a duty, and hold new moves while you type in chat. - **Train party**: accepts party invites during a ride so the party shares mark credit, can shout for a group at the start, and leaves the party when the ride is over. - **GM alert**: ends the ride when a GM is near, with optional toast, beeps, or custom commands. - **History**: every train recorded with world, data center, marks credited, time on the rails, and seals earned. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Auto Hunt Train**, and install. The plugin needs a few helpers to be installed and loaded: movement, combat, travel through Lifestream, and HuntAlerts for the train announcements. Open `/aht deps` after install to see the list and one-click each missing one. Data center rides also need data center travel enabled in Lifestream's own settings. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/aht` | Toggle the main window | | `/hunttrain` | Alias for `/aht` | | `/aht config` | Open the Settings page | | `/aht stats` | Open the History page | | `/aht deps` | Open the Plugins page | | `/aht log` | Open the Console page | | `/aht changelog` | Open the Changelog page | | `/aht about` | Open the About page | | `/aht pause` | Pause or resume the current ride | | `/aht conductor [@World]` | Follow this player's flags; the world defaults to yours. Alone, shows the current conductor | | `/aht conductor clear` | Stop following anyone | | `/aht snooze []` | Suspend auto-join and the train notifications for the snooze length set in Settings, or for the minutes given | | `/aht snooze off` | Lift the snooze | | `/aht inject [] [i] [+] [conductor:] [body:]` | Push a made-up train announcement through the same intake as HuntAlerts, on a world in any region, so the rules, the details and the whole ride can be tried with no real train, e.g. `/aht inject Raiden DT Wachunpelo +5 conductor:Pandora Rainfall`. Everything after `body:` is the Discord post, with `\n` for a line break (debug helper) | | `/aht target` | Log targeted NPC's BaseId (debug helper) | | `/aht goto ` | Travel to a point, `/aht goto stop` cancels (debug helper) | | `/aht goto [] [i]` | Travel to a world in your region, and on it to a named aetheryte and instance, e.g. `/aht goto Zalera Wachunpelo i2` (debug helper) | | `/aht goto home` | Travel back to your home world (debug helper) | ## Languages The windows are available in English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, 日本語, and 中文. website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto Sightseeing Log

Sightseeing vistas, logged for you. Built on Dalamud.

---

## What it does Lists every Sightseeing Log vista from A Realm Reborn through Dawntrail in one window, grouped by expansion and zone. Tick the vistas you want and press **Start**: the plugin teleports and flies to each one, waits for its hour and weather when it has them, performs the emote the log asks for, and moves on until every vista you picked is in your log. ## Features - **The whole log**: all 340 vistas from A Realm Reborn through Dawntrail, grouped by zone, with the ones you haven't unlocked yet locked and what opens them one hover away. - **Live log progress**: reads which vistas you have logged straight from the game, so the window always matches your Sightseeing Log. - **Time and weather windows**: works out when each A Realm Reborn vista's Eorzean hour and weather line up, and counts down to when it opens or closes. - **Smart ordering**: visits open vistas before they close and lines up the rest for when their window opens. - **Travel**: teleports to the nearest aetheryte and flies or walks to the spot, including the vistas whose marker sits where you can't stand. - **Jump puzzles**: climbs the city jump puzzles it has a route for (Bokairo Inn and Shiokaze Hostelry in Kugane, Ruveydah Fibers Rooftop Garden in Radz-at-Han, Hunu'iliy in Tuliyollal), picks the climb back up after a missed jump, and leaves the puzzles it has no route for to you. - **The right emote**: performs /lookout, /pray, /comfort or whichever emote each vista asks for, and checks that the log recorded it. - **Hard spots**: when a vista sits on something the plugin cannot get onto by itself, it marks the spot in the world, points an arrow at it from above your character, flashes the game in your taskbar if you are in another window, and waits up to a minute for you to stand inside before carrying on. Turn it off in Settings for unattended runs. Settings also has when the box and the arrow show (always, near the spot, only when it needs you, or never) and how large the arrow is. - **Recovery**: re-paths, jumps, side-steps, or teleports out when it gets stuck on the way, and waits out a fight before it emotes. - **After the run**: stay where you are, return to the inn, log out to title, or close the game once a run finishes by itself. - **Pause & resume**: park a run without losing your progress, and auto-pause while you're in a duty. - **History**: every run recorded with the vistas logged and the zones visited. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Auto Sightseeing Log**, and install. The plugin needs a helper for movement to be installed and loaded. Open `/asl deps` after install to see it and install it in one click. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/asl` | Toggle the main window | | `/sightseeing` | Alias for `/asl` | | `/asl config` | Open the Settings page | | `/asl stats` | Open the History page | | `/asl deps` | Open the Plugins page | | `/asl about` | Open the About page | | `/asl pause` | Pause or resume the current run | | `/asl goto ` | Travel to a vista without logging it (debug helper); `/asl goto stop` cancels | | `/asl logdump` | Write the Sightseeing Log state to the plugin log (debug helper) | ## Languages The windows are available in English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, 日本語, and 中文. The plugin picks a language from your Dalamud and game client settings on first launch; change it any time under Settings, General, Language. Game data such as zone, vista, emote, and weather names always follows the game client. Spotted a wrong or awkward translation? Open a [translation issue](https://github.com/XeldarAlz/FFXIV-AutoSightseeingLog/issues/new?template=translation_report.yml) and tell me what it should say instead. ## More from me If you liked this plugin, take a look at my other Dalamud work. You might find something else there for you. → [XeldarAlz Dalamud Plugins](https://github.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins) ## License AGPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md). website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto Triple Triad Grind

Every NPC card, collected for you. Built on Dalamud.

--- ## What it does Lists every Triple Triad card an NPC can give you, which ones you already own, and which NPCs drop each one. Pick single cards, whole NPCs, or every card you are missing, and press **Start**: the plugin plans a route, travels to each NPC, builds a deck for that NPC's rules, plays match after match until every card you picked from them has dropped, registers the cards, and moves on to the next NPC. ## Features - **Card collection view**: every NPC reward card from A Realm Reborn through Dawntrail, grouped by expansion, by NPC or by card, with owned cards checked off. - **Pick what you want**: click a card to pick it, click an NPC to pick everything you are missing from them, or pick every missing card at once. - **Route planning**: each card goes to the NPC that also gives the most of your other picks, and NPCs are visited zone by zone so a run teleports as little as possible. - **Deck building**: an optimized deck is built for each NPC from your own cards and that NPC's rules, including regional rules, or you can play one of your saved decks. - **Auto-play**: plays every turn with a match solver that knows all sixteen rules, then asks for a rematch until the NPC has nothing left to give. - **Card registration**: won cards are registered straight away, and the run pauses before your bags fill up. - **Farm mode**: pick one or more NPCs and play them a set number of times or until you stop. - **Skips instead of stalls**: locked NPCs, NPCs you keep losing to, and NPCs asking a higher fee than you allow are skipped and listed with the reason. - **After-run action**: stay where you are, return to the inn, log out, or close the game once the route is done. - **Pause & resume**: park a run without losing your progress, and auto-pause while you're in a duty. - **Party invites**: auto-declines incoming invites during a run after a random delay, with an optional reply message. - **GM alert**: stops the bot when a GM is near, with optional toast, beeps, or custom commands. - **History**: every run recorded with matches won, NPCs finished, and the cards you got. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Auto Triple Triad Grind**, and install. The plugin needs a movement helper to be installed and loaded. Open `/attg deps` after install to see it and install it with one click. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/attg` | Toggle the main window | | `/tripletriad` | Alias for `/attg` | | `/attg config` | Open the Settings page | | `/attg stats` | Open the History page | | `/attg deps` | Open the Plugins page | | `/attg log` | Open the Console page | | `/attg changelog` | Open the Changelog page | | `/attg about` | Open the About page | | `/attg pause` | Pause or resume the current run | | `/attg npcs` | Write the Triple Triad NPC table to the plugin log (debug helper) | | `/attg board` | Print what the plugin reads off an open match board (debug helper) | | `/attg request` | Print the regional rules read off an open challenge window (debug helper) | | `/attg goto ` | Travel to a point, `/attg goto stop` cancels (debug helper) | ## Languages The windows are available in English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, 日本語, and 中文. The plugin picks a language from your Dalamud and game client settings on first launch; change it any time under Settings, General, Language. Game data such as card, NPC, and zone names always follows the game client. Spotted a wrong or awkward translation? website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto Treasure Maps

Treasure maps, dug up for you. Built on Dalamud.

--- ## What it does Works through the timeworn maps in your bags for you. Press **Start** and the plugin deciphers a map, travels to its dig spot, digs up the coffer, fights off the monsters that guard it, opens it, and moves on to the next map until your bags are empty. Once they are, it can gather the day's free map and buy more on the market board, if you turn those on. Portals and undersea maps are left to you. ## Features - **Decipher and dig**: reads each timeworn map you carry, works out where it points, and digs at the spot. - **Travel**: teleports to the nearest aetheryte, then flies, rides or walks to the dig spot, and lands where it can dig. - **Hands-off combat**: fights off every wave that guards a coffer with a bundled combat preset, then opens the coffer. - **Map choice**: pick which map tiers to run and whether the highest or the lowest goes first. - **Loot rolls**: answers the Need or Greed window for the coffer's items the way you choose, or leaves it to you. - **Daily map**: once a day, gathers the free timeworn map as a Miner or Botanist when the run has no map left, then switches back to your gearset (off by default). A Miner skips Gargantuaskin, whose only Miner nodes hold nothing but collectables. - **Market board**: when no map is left in your bags and no daily map can be gathered, buys the next one on the market board under a price cap you set per tier, within a gil budget per run and never below the gil you choose to keep (off by default). - **Recovery**: gets back up after a death; re-paths, jumps, or teleports out when it gets stuck. - **After-run action**: stay logged in, return to the inn, log out, or close the game once the last map is done. - **Auto-repair**: Dark Matter first, then your Grand Company mender or a repair NPC you pick. - **Auto-consume**: keeps food and medicine buffs up between maps, HQ first. - **Humanizer**: waits a random moment before each teleport, dig, coffer and fight, and takes city breaks between maps, so long sessions look less mechanical. - **Pause & resume**: park a run without losing your place, and auto-pause while you're in a duty. - **Party invites**: auto-declines incoming invites during a run after a random delay, with an optional reply message. - **GM alert**: stops the bot when a GM is near, with optional toast, beeps, or custom commands. - **Stop conditions**: a run ends when no enabled map is left, after a set number of maps or minutes, after failed maps in a row, or after a second knockout. - **History**: every run recorded with its maps, gil (less what it spent on maps), portals seen and how it ended. - **Console**: a live log of every step, with filters and a copy button for bug reports. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Auto Treasure Maps**, and install. The plugin needs a few helpers for movement and combat to be installed and loaded. Open `/atm deps` after install to see the list and one-click each missing one. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/atm` | Toggle the main window | | `/treasuremaps` | Alias for `/atm` | | `/atm config` | Open the Settings page | | `/atm stats` | Open the History page | | `/atm deps` | Open the Plugins page | | `/atm log` | Open the Console page | | `/atm changelog` | Open the Changelog page | | `/atm about` | Open the About page | | `/atm start` | Start a run: decipher and run your maps until a stop condition | | `/atm stop` | Stop the current run | | `/atm pause` | Pause or resume the current run | | `/atm target` | Log targeted object's BaseId (debug helper) | | `/atm spot` | Print the deciphered map you hold and its dig spot | | `/atm flag` | Flag that dig spot on the map | | `/atm goto spot` | Travel to that dig spot and land on it | | `/atm dig` | Run the held map: travel, dig, fight the guards, loot the coffer | | `/atm decipher [map]` | Decipher the next timeworn map in your bags by the order in Settings, or the one named (a piece of its name or its item id) | | `/atm buy [map]` | Buy the next map on the market board under its price cap, or the one named (a piece of its name or its item id); market buying must be on in Settings, Maps | | `/atm gather` | Gather today's timeworn map once as a Miner or Botanist, `/atm gather stop` cancels | | `/atm tiers` | List every map tier in the Console (debug helper) | | `/atm goto ` | Travel to a point, `/atm goto stop` cancels (debug helper) | ## Languages The windows are available in English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, 日本語, and 中文. The plugin picks a language from your Dalamud and game client settings on first launch; change it any time under Settings, General, Language. website.title: FFXIV-AutoShopper
website.description: Your market board shopping list, bought for you
website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto Shopper

Your market board shopping list, bought for you. Built on Dalamud.

--- ## What it does Write down what you want from the market board, and Auto Shopper works out where to buy it. It reads Universalis prices for the worlds you allow, plans the cheapest mix of whole listings, travels there with Lifestream, walks to the market board, and buys within the caps you set, confirming every purchase before it counts. Dry run is on until you switch it off: a dry run does everything except send the purchase, so you can watch a whole run and check its numbers against the board before any gil is spent. ## Features - **Shopping lists**: search any item sold on the market board by name or id, then set its quality (Any, HQ or NQ), whether to buy a set amount or top up to what you want to own, the most it may pay per unit with the 5% market fee included, and how many extra units it may take when only bigger stacks are listed. Owned counts cover your bags, crystals, armory chest and equipped gear. Lists are kept between sessions and can be renamed, duplicated and archived. - **Imports**: paste plain text such as `3x Darksteel Ore`, a CSV, an Auto Shopper JSON export, an Artisan crafting list or a Teamcraft list. A crafting list is bought as finished items, as its direct ingredients, or expanded down to the raw materials. Nothing changes until you choose to add the rows, replace the list or start a new one. - **Crystal helper**: pick elements and kinds (shards, crystals, clusters) and they become Top up lines, so a run buys only what your crystal bag is missing. - **Exports**: lists as text, CSV or JSON, plans as a text or Markdown checklist, and run summaries as text or JSON. None of them hold character names, content ids, retainers or listing ids. - **Universalis prices**: Get prices on the Plan page reads the current listings of the list's items on the worlds you allow, chosen from a preset (current world, home data center, current data center, or whole region) and a world picker. Prices older than the age you set are flagged. - **Three plan modes**: Cheapest, Balanced (weighs the total against the stop and data center penalties you set) and Fewest stops (the fewest worlds, within a premium over the cheapest). The Plan page compares all three on the same prices and shows the route in visit order, the estimated total with the fee, your budget against the spend cap, price freshness, and every unit it could not place with the reason why. Plans buy whole listings only. - **Travel**: world changes and data center transfers through Lifestream. A transfer logs the character out and back in, and the run carries on by itself afterwards. On each world it takes the aethernet when that is shorter and walks to a market board, in your preferred city when none is in reach. - **Live listings at every stop**: the run searches each item on the board itself and plans what is left again from those listings, so a stale Universalis price never decides a purchase. - **Guarded purchases**: every purchase is checked before it is sent, written to a journal, and confirmed against the server's answer and the change in your gil and bags. See [Safety](#safety). - **Uncertain purchases**: a purchase without a clear answer stops all buying and puts a card on the Shop page with your gil and owned count before and after, so you can say whether it went through. - **Run controls**: Start, Pause, Resume and Stop on the Shop page or as commands, auto-pause while you're in a duty, hold new moves while you type in chat, and auto-resume after an unexpected error (up to 3 times in 5 minutes). - **Way home**: when a run ends on its own, back to your home world, crossing data centers when needed, then an optional after-run action (stay, return to the inn, log out, or close the game). A Stop or a fault runs neither, and logging out and closing the game are skipped after a dry run. - **Humanizer**: short random delays before the character moves off or casts a teleport. - **GM alert**: ends a run when a GM is near, with an optional toast, chat line, beeps, custom commands, or closing the game. - **History and console**: every run recorded with its outcome, list, world, data center, units, gil and time, with a summary to copy for each real run and for the last dry run. Every step is logged on the Console page, ready to copy into a bug report. ## How a run works 1. Pick a list on the Shop page and press **Start** (or type `/ashop start`). The run gets fresh prices, makes the plan, and checks that a run spend cap is set. 2. It travels to the first stop through Lifestream, changing world or data center as the plan needs. 3. It takes the aethernet if that is shorter, walks to a market board and opens it. 4. For each item on that stop it reads the live listings and plans what is left again from what the board shows. 5. Each chosen listing passes the purchase checks, is written to the journal, and is bought, one at a time. In a dry run it is logged as "would buy" instead. 6. It waits for the answer and checks your gil and bags, then moves on to the next item and the next stop. 7. When the list is covered, the cap is reached or nothing affordable is left, it travels home (when Return home is on), runs the after-run action, and records the run in History. ## Safety - **Dry run by default.** A dry run travels, searches and checks like a real run, but never sends a purchase; each one is logged as "would buy" with its price, and its journal stays in memory. The Dry run switch sits next to Start. Switching it on takes one click; switching it off asks first and says that real gil will be spent. - **Caps.** No run starts without a run spend cap. Each line can have its own most per unit (fee included) and its allowance for extra units, a run always leaves the gil you choose to keep in your purse, and Most stops limits how many worlds a plan visits. - **Every purchase is checked** before it is sent: the right character, on an allowed world it is standing on, the same item, quality and stack size as the listing chosen, a line that still needs units, the line's cap, the run's budget, the gil you keep, room in your bags or crystal pouch, unique items you already own, and no other purchase waiting for an answer. - **Refusals.** Listings from your own retainers, items on a mannequin, and set listings are never bought. - **Journal first.** The purchase is written to the purchase journal on disk before it is sent; when that write fails, nothing is sent. - **Confirmed, not assumed.** A purchase counts only when the server's answer agrees with the game's purchase events and your purse and bags changed by what they should. Anything less stops buying and asks you on the Shop page. - **One purchase at a time.** Never more than one purchase waits for an answer, and Stop waits for that answer before it ends the run. - **Interrupted runs.** A run cut short by a logout or a reload never resumes on its own: the Shop page offers to resume it with fresh prices or to discard it, and Resume is refused while dry run is on. A journal that cannot be trusted keeps buying off until you set it aside. - **What it never does**: sell or list items, touch your retainers, travel outside your home region, buy more than your list asks for beyond the extra units you allow, spend past the run spend cap or below the gil you keep, or send a purchase in a dry run. The only network traffic it makes itself is reading prices from Universalis. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Auto Shopper**, and install. ## Requirements - **Lifestream** for world and data center travel. Runs that cross data centers also need data center travel turned on in Lifestream's own settings (`/li`). - **vnavmesh** for walking to the market board. - A **run spend cap** under Settings, Shopping. Plans work without one; runs do not start. Open `/ashop deps` after install to see both helpers and one-click each missing one. `/ashop mbstatus` says whether the market board can be read and bought on your game version; when buying is off, only dry runs start. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/ashop` | Toggle the main window | | `/shopper` | Alias for `/ashop` | | `/ashop config` | Open the Settings page | | `/ashop stats` | Open the History page (`/ashop history` works too) | | `/ashop deps` | Open the Plugins page (`/ashop dependencies` works too) | | `/ashop log` | Open the Console page | | `/ashop changelog` | Open the Changelog page | | `/ashop about` | Open the About page | | `/ashop add [quantity]` | Add a Buy line at Any quality to the selected list, making a list first when there is none | | `/ashop start` | Start a run of the selected list (a dry run while dry run is on) | | `/ashop stop` | Stop the run; a purchase already sent is answered first | | `/ashop pause` | Pause or resume the current run (`/ashop resume` works too) | | `/ashop look ` | Log every listing of one item at the market board in reach; it never buys (debug helper) | | `/ashop mbstatus` | Report whether the market board checks of this game version pass (debug helper) | | `/ashop board [city]` | Go to a market board and open it, in the given city (limsa, gridania, uldah, ishgard, kugane, crystarium, sharlayan, tuliyollal) or the preferred one (debug helper) | | `/ashop board stop` | Cancel the trip to a market board (debug helper) | | `/ashop target` | Log targeted NPC's BaseId (debug helper) | | `/ashop goto ` | Travel to a point (debug helper) | | `/ashop goto [] [i]` | Travel to a world in your region, and on it to a named aetheryte and instance, e.g. `/ashop goto Zalera Wachunpelo i2` (debug helper) | | `/ashop goto home` | Travel back to your home world (debug helper) | | `/ashop goto stop` | Cancel a goto (debug helper) | ## Known limits - **Universalis is an estimate.** Its prices come from player uploads and can lag behind the board, or miss a world nobody uploaded lately, and a world sends only its 100 cheapest listings. website.title: FFXIV-AutoGCSupply
website.description: Grand Company supply and provisioning, delivered for you.
website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto GC Supply

Grand Company supply and provisioning, delivered for you. Built on Dalamud.

--- ## What it does Every day your Grand Company asks for crafted and gathered items in exchange for experience and company seals. Auto GC Supply reads the day's supply and provisioning requests, shows what each one costs and pays, and with one button buys what you are missing, travels to your Personnel Officer and hands in the requests you chose, confirming every delivery. It never buys anything itself. Every purchase goes through Auto Shopper (1.1.0.0 or later), under Auto Shopper's own caps and purchase checks, and Auto Shopper's dry run covers the whole run: while it is on, a run buys nothing and hands nothing in, and every step shows what it would do. Without Auto Shopper the plugin still hands in what your bags already hold, and those hand-ins are real. ## Features - **Today page**: the day's 8 supply requests (crafting classes) and 3 provisioning requests (gathering classes), each with its item and quantity, how many NQ and HQ you hold in your bags, the experience it pays and its share of your current level, the seals it pays, the estimated cost of what is missing, and the gil it costs per 1,000 experience. Above the list: your Grand Company rank, your seals against your rank's cap, the time to the next reset, Auto Shopper's state and dry run, and totals for what you chose, with the estimated spend and any seals the cap would cost you. - **Smaller windows**: requests switch to stacked cards when the table columns no longer fit. Shopper controls wrap, the spend-cap label stays above its controls, and readiness details wrap onto additional lines. The expanded window keeps a usable minimum width; collapsing it still allows a compact header. - **Reading the requests**: the game sends the day's requests only once its Timers window has been opened, so Auto GC Supply opens it for a moment when it needs them, and reads them again after the daily reset at 20:00 UTC. Refresh on the Grand Company card reads them again on demand. - **Pick what to do**: click a row to include or leave out its class, or use All and None for each group. Your choices are kept per character. Classes at the level cap start left out, since they earn seals only; Include max-level classes under Settings, Run brings them in. - **Quality that pays**: HQ supply turn-ins pay double experience and seals, so Automatic quality buys the HQ item when it costs at most twice the NQ one, and when your bags already cover a request, it hands in HQ before NQ. Always HQ and Always NQ are there too. Provisioning is always bought and handed in as NQ. - **Prices through Auto Shopper**: the Today page asks Auto Shopper for the market price of what is missing, on the worlds Auto Shopper may visit. Each line's price cap is the dearest listing unit price that quote chose, plus the price tolerance you set (25% by default, up to 200%). A fresh quote right before buying can lower a cap or drop a line with no listings, never raise a cap. - **Run spend cap**: any run that buys needs one. The Today page says whether it covers the estimate and offers the estimate plus 20% in one click. Auto Shopper never spends past it. - **One button**: Automate (or `/gcsupply start`) buys the missing items through Auto Shopper, travels to your Grand Company, hands in each chosen request at the Personnel Officer, and checks every delivery. See [How a run works](#how-a-run-works). - **Guarded hand-in**: the officer's menu is chosen by its text, rows are matched by item and class, the reward window is checked before Deliver, and every delivery is confirmed. See [Safety](#safety). - **Seal cap**: when a request's seals would pass your rank's cap, deliver anyway for the experience (the default) or skip the row and keep the item. - **Run view**: a step rail (Reading, Pricing, Buying, Travelling, Handing in, Done), Auto Shopper's spend while it buys, every row's state and reason, and a summary card at the end with the requests delivered, the gil spent and the time taken. When a run needs you, a card says why and what to do next. - **Run controls**: Pause, Resume and Stop in the dock at the bottom of the window or as commands, auto-pause while you are in a duty, and hold new moves while you type in chat. While Auto Shopper is buying, pausing belongs to Auto Shopper; Stop asks it to stop, and the run ends once its purchase settles. - **Humanizer**: short random delays before the character moves off or casts a teleport. - **GM alert**: ends a run when a GM is near, with an optional toast, chat line, beeps, custom commands, or closing the game. - **History and console**: the last 200 runs with their outcome, requests delivered, experience, seals, seals lost to the cap and gil spent, with dry runs marked. Every step is logged on the Console page, ready to copy into a bug report. ## How a run works 1. Choose the requests you want on the Today page, set a run spend cap when anything needs buying, and press **Automate** (or type `/gcsupply start`). Automate starts only when you are logged in, in a Grand Company, on your home world and outside a duty, with today's requests loaded and, when anything needs buying, priced. The run keeps to the rows and caps you saw at that moment. 2. It reads the day's requests again and drops any row that was handed in elsewhere or changed since. 3. When something is missing, it gets fresh prices from Auto Shopper if the last ones are older than 10 minutes, then sends Auto Shopper one order: each missing item, its quality and price cap, and the run spend cap. Auto Shopper buys under its own rules and travels back to your home world. The first time, the run stops here: Auto Shopper asks you on its Shop page to allow Auto GC Supply, and you press Automate again once you have. 4. It counts your bags, teleports to your Grand Company's city, takes the aethernet when that is shorter, and walks to the Personnel Officer. 5. It opens the supply list from the officer's menu, fills the item request with the chosen quality from your bags, and presses Hand Over before checking the reward window. It confirms each delivery before picking the next request. In a dry run it stops short of choosing a row and marks each one it would hand in. 6. It closes the officer's windows and records the run in History. ## Safety - **Every purchase belongs to Auto Shopper.** Auto GC Supply never touches the market board. It sends Auto Shopper one order per run, with a price cap on each line and the run spend cap, and Auto Shopper's worlds, gil reserve and purchase checks still apply. - **Dry run.** Auto Shopper's Dry run switch, shown next to Automate, governs the whole run. While it is on, nothing is bought and nothing is handed in: the run travels, opens the supply list, and marks each row it would deliver. When Auto Shopper 1.1.0.0 or later is there but its switch cannot be read, the hand-in is dry too. Without Auto Shopper there is no dry run, so a hand-in-only run delivers for real. An Auto Shopper that is installed but older than 1.1.0.0, or newer than this version understands, keeps Automate off until one of them is updated, so its dry run is never skipped. - **Asked once.** The first run that buys stops at Auto Shopper's permission card on its Shop page, and nothing is bought until you allow Auto GC Supply there. You can take that back under Auto Shopper's Settings, General. - **Caps.** No run that buys starts without a run spend cap, and each line carries its own price cap. - **Only the rows you chose.** A run hands in only the rows you had chosen at Start, and drops a row whose request changed or was handed in elsewhere. - **Menu by text.** The officer's supply option is found by its text, read from the game data in your client's language, never by its place in the menu. - **Rows by item and class.** A row is handed in only when exactly one row of the supply list shows that item for that class, its amount matches the request the run started with, the game still takes it, and your bags hold enough of the chosen quality. - **One row at a time.** It hands in one request, waits for its confirmation, and only then picks the next. - **Item request checked before Hand Over.** The requested item and quantity must match the selected mission. The offered items must have the chosen quality and quantity, including when another helper filled the request. A mismatch cancels the request. - **Reward window checked before Deliver.** The item and the seals in the reward window must match the request (seals may run higher with the star and seal bonuses, or lower near your seal cap). An HQ hand-in may still display the base seal reward; that is accepted only after the offered items or the HQ confirmation independently establish the quality. Delivery is still checked against the HQ bag count. Anything else is cancelled and the run stops. - **Only the HQ trade prompt.** The one question it answers Yes to is the game's prompt to trade a high-quality item, and only on an HQ row, once. Any other question is answered No and the run stops; an unexpected window stops it too. - **Confirmed, not assumed.** A delivery counts only when your bags dropped by the requested amount and your seals rose (or the row left the list). Anything less marks it unconfirmed, and the run asks you to check the supply list. - **Stops for you.** Combat, a duty pop, an officer it cannot find or reach, a list that does not open, or a hand-in that takes too long ends the run with a card that says why. Press Automate to try again once you have checked the game. A logout or a reload ends the run, and nothing resumes on its own. - **What it never does**: buy anything itself, sell or list items, accept a prompt it does not know, hand in a row you did not choose, spend past the run spend cap, or deliver while Auto Shopper's dry run is on. It makes no network calls of its own; prices come through Auto Shopper. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Auto GC Supply**, and install. ## Requirements - **vnavmesh** for walking to the Personnel Officer. Automate stays off until it is installed and loaded. - **Auto Shopper 1.1.0.0 or later** for buying the missing items, through its Buying API. It is optional: without it, only requests your bags already cover are handed in, and there is no dry run. Once it is installed, Automate stays off while it is older than 1.1.0.0 or newer than this version understands. The first run that buys asks you once, on Auto Shopper's Shop page, to allow Auto GC Supply; press Allow there, then press Automate again. Auto Shopper brings its own requirements, such as Lifestream for its trips between worlds. - **A Grand Company**, with runs started from your home world. - **A run spend cap** on the Today page or under Settings, Run, for any run that buys. Open `/gcsupply deps` after install to see the helpers and one-click each missing one. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/gcsupply` | Toggle the main window | | `/agcs` | Alias for `/gcsupply` | | `/gcsupply config` | Open the Settings page | | `/gcsupply stats` | Open the History page (`/gcsupply history` works too) | | `/gcsupply deps` | Open the Plugins page (`/gcsupply dependencies` works too) | | `/gcsupply log` | Open the Console page | | `/gcsupply changelog` | Open the Changelog page | | `/gcsupply about` | Open the About page | | `/gcsupply start` | Open the Today page and start a run of the chosen requests; when it cannot start, the chat says why | | `/gcsupply stop` | Stop the run; while Auto Shopper is buying, it is asked to stop and the run ends once it settles | | `/gcsupply pause` | Pause or resume the current run (`/gcsupply resume` works too); while Auto Shopper is buying, pause it there | | `/gcsupply target` | Log the targeted NPC's BaseId (debug helper) | ## Known limits - **Bags only.** Owned counts and hand-ins use your four inventory bags. The armoury chest, equipped gear, retainers and saddlebags are never counted or used. - **Provisioning is NQ only.** HQ copies in your bags are not handed in for a provisioning request, and the row offers to buy NQ instead. - **The Timers window opens by itself** for a moment when today's requests have not reached the game yet. - **Runs close to the daily reset.** When 20:00 UTC passes before the buying, nothing is bought. When it passes after, only requests that still match are handed in, and what was bought for the others stays in your bags. - **Extra units.** When only bigger stacks are listed, Auto Shopper may buy up to as many extra units as a request asks for (requests of 2 or more), within the price caps and the run spend cap. The extras stay in your bags. - **Prices are estimates.** They are Auto Shopper's Universalis prices, and Auto Shopper's own known limits apply to every purchase. ## Languages The windows are available in English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, 日本語, and 中文. The plugin picks a language from your Dalamud and game client settings on first launch; change it any time under Settings, General, Language. Game data such as zone, item, and world names always follows the game client. Spotted a wrong or awkward translation? Open a [translation issue](https://github.com/XeldarAlz/FFXIV-AutoGCSupply/issues/new?template=translation_report.yml) and tell me what it should say instead. ## Community Questions, ideas, or just want to hang out with other players? Come say hi on Discord. → [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/hppkAvdBEE) ## More from me If you liked this plugin, take a look at my other Dalamud work. You might find something else there for you. → [XeldarAlz Dalamud Plugins](https://github.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins) ## License AGPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md). website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto House Lottery

Find an empty plot, enter its housing lottery, collect your refund or claim your house. Built on Dalamud.

--- ## What it does Shows empty housing plots on a map from public listings, enters the lottery on the plot you pick or the best match on your shortlist, then checks the result and collects your refund or claims your house. Pick a plot and press **Enter**, or build a shortlist and press **Enter best match**. The plugin travels there, reads the placard, checks the plot, buyer type and deposit, and enters once per character, as the game allows. ## Features - **Find a home**: vacant plots for any world on the district map and in a list, filtered by district, ward, size, price, buyer type and lottery phase. - **Shortlist**: collect the plots you would accept, one at a time or every matching plot at once. - **Enter best match**: ranks your shortlist by open entry, fewest entries and lowest deposit, and enters the first plot that still passes the live checks. - **Run panel**: follow each step with Pause and Stop, in the window or a compact strip. - **My lottery**: your entries with deposit, lottery number and deadline, and one button each to check the result, claim the house or collect the refund. - **Several characters**: tick characters on the Characters list and press **Enter for N characters** to enter once for each, every one paying from its own gil. Characters that can claim only one plot between them are kept on the same plot, and Lifestream logs in each character in turn. - **Automatic refunds**: once results are out and you are idle, visits your entered plots and reads their results, within a travel budget and your gil reserve. With **Switch characters to collect refunds** on, it then logs in your other ticked characters that have a result waiting. - **Saved**: named searches and plot lists, with notices when a plot opens for entry, is about to close, or has results. - **Safe by design**: checks the plot at the placard and again on the confirmation, records every press before making it, and never presses twice when an outcome is unclear. - **GM alert**: ends a run when a GM is near, with optional pop-up, beeps, or custom commands. ## Multiple characters Tick characters on the Characters list in the shortlist drawer and the drawer plans exactly the ticked ones (with none ticked it plans the logged-in character as before). Each character makes at most one entry per lottery period and pays from its own gil; nothing is pooled. - **Characters list**: every character the plugin has seen logged in. Give each ticked character its own buyer type, target (the best match or one plot of the shortlist on its home world), deposit cap and reserve; anything left blank takes the filters' buyer type, the price ceiling and the shared reserve. A character that is not logged in shows the gil it had at its last login, marked as an estimate: that amount never proves or rules out that it can pay. Characters that already entered this period, or whose home world is not supported, say so. - **Ownership groups**: the game lets only one plot be claimed per Free Company for Free Company plots, and per service account and home world for private plots. Set each character's service account on the Characters list; until you do, private characters on one world count as one account, which can never produce a second win that cannot be claimed. - **Placement**: By group (the default) puts a group's characters on the same plot and spreads separate groups across the shortlist in rank order; Same plot puts every group on the top plot; Spread gives each character the next plot. A character's own target is entered exactly, with no fallback, and the rest of its group goes on that plot too, with no fallback; a member that cannot enter it, or whose own target is another plot, is left out with that reason. A character that already entered this period, or has an entry being checked, holds its group on its plot the same way, and one whose entered plot could not be read leaves the rest of its group out. When a member enters, or its own check finds it already entered, the members of its group still waiting are pinned to that plot, and any whose plan does not include it are left out, so under By group or Same plot a group never enters two plots. While a member's entry is being checked, the rest of its group waits, and the batch card says so, until a Continue reads it back from the journal; other groups go on meanwhile. Next to Placement the run preview shows the estimated chance of at least one win and, when Spread puts one group on several plots, of two or more wins, from the reported entry counts; it is hidden when any count is unknown. Spreading inside one group needs your explicit confirmation that only one of its wins can be claimed. - **Enter for N characters**: every character goes through exactly the same steps and checks as a single run, including the check for a plugin that answers dialogs on its own before each Enter Lottery, and pays its own deposit. The logged-in character goes first; right before its turn each character's gil is checked against its whole target order, and its run reads its lottery record before anything else. The batch then logs in each of the others in turn (see [Character switching](#character-switching)); when Lifestream cannot switch, they wait for their own login: log in with one of them and press **Continue** on the batch card (the chat reminds you); the card says why when Continue cannot go on. The batch card lists every character's outcome with the entries first, so characters that were left out, could not pay or have not logged in yet never hide the entries the others made. A new batch is refused while one still waits; continue it or discard it. The batch ends with the entry period. - **Several wins in one group**: My lottery asks you to choose which plot to claim (press Claim house twice on the one you want); a second claim in that group is always refused. ### Character switching The plugin switches characters itself through Lifestream's character change, for batches and, with its option on, for collecting refunds. When Lifestream does not offer it, a batch processes only the logged-in character and every other character waits for its own login, and each character's results and refunds are handled at its own login. The Plugins page (`/ahl deps`) shows whether switching is available. Before a switch, a batch saves its progress to disk, asks Lifestream to log in the next character, and does nothing for it until the game shows exactly that character (content ID and home world) and Lifestream has finished; its gil, Free Company and estates are then read again and its run reads its lottery record before anything else. No switch starts during a duty, match or world visit queue, while vnavmesh is moving you, or while AutoRetainer's multi-mode is on. The switch has a five-minute deadline; a failed login, another character chosen at the character screen, a cancel, or a plugin reload on the title screen stops the batch, and a stopped or reloaded batch continues only from your Continue. **Switch characters to collect refunds** on My lottery (off by default) lets the refund queue, once the logged-in character has nothing left to settle and you have left the game alone, log in the next character ticked on the Characters list that has a result waiting and check it there. Each character is visited once until the plugin is unloaded, never an unticked character and never one whose home world is not supported. The plugin passes only a character name and world to Lifestream and stores no account credentials. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Auto House Lottery**, and install. The plugin needs **Lifestream** to travel to plots, and optionally **vnavmesh** to walk up to the placard. Open `/ahl deps` after install to see the list and one-click each missing one. YesAlready can stay on: the plugin pauses it while it works with the lottery dialogs and resumes it afterwards. Chinese and Korean worlds are not supported. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/autohouselottery` | Toggle the main window | | `/ahl` | Alias for `/autohouselottery` | | `/autohouselottery config` | Open the Settings page | | `/autohouselottery lottery` | Open the My lottery page | | `/autohouselottery saved` | Open the Saved page | | `/autohouselottery deps` | Open the Plugins page (`/autohouselottery dependencies` works too) | | `/autohouselottery log` | Open the Console page (live plugin log, copy it for bug reports) | | `/autohouselottery changelog` | Open the Changelog page | | `/autohouselottery about` | Open the About page | | `/autohouselottery stop` | Stop the run, a result visit or a batch before its next step | | `/autohouselottery pause` | Pause the run before its next step | | `/autohouselottery resume` | Resume a paused run, or continue a waiting batch | | `/autohouselottery target` | Log the targeted object's BaseId (debug helper) | Testing and maintainer commands are in [docs/testing-commands.md](docs/testing-commands.md). ## Privacy Listings come from the public housing service at `housing-api.yozoracho.dev`. The requests carry only the plugin's name and version, nothing about you or your characters, and what the plugin reads from the game stays on your machine. ## Languages The windows are available in English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, 日本語, and 中文. The plugin picks a language from your Dalamud and game client settings on first launch; change it any time under Settings, General, Language. Game data such as world, district and zone names always follows the game client. Spotted a wrong or awkward translation? Open a [translation issue](https://github.com/XeldarAlz/FFXIV-AutoHouseLottery/issues/new?template=translation_report.yml) and tell me what it should say instead. ## Community Questions, ideas, or just want to hang out with other players? Come say hi on Discord. → [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/hppkAvdBEE) ## More from me If you liked this plugin, take a look at my other Dalamud work. You might find something else there for you. → [XeldarAlz Dalamud Plugins](https://github.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins) ## License AGPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md). website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto Seller

Your retainer listings, sold for you. Built on Dalamud.

--- ## What it does Shows your retainers' listings and everything in your bags in one list. For each row choose what happens: keep a listing the cheapest, give it your own price, or sell an item on the market board or to an NPC. Press **Sell now** or **Undercut now** and the plugin goes to a summoning bell and does it all in one trip, or switch on **Autopilot** to have it done on its own while you are idle. Nothing new is listed until you tick it, no price goes below its floor, and every sale is recorded. ## Features - **Sell page**: your listings and how they stand, everything you carry that can be sold, and one-click buttons per row: Undercut, My price, Market board or NPC. - **Autopilot**: every hour, 2 hours or 4 hours, only once you have stood still outside combat, duties and cutscenes, or after each AutoRetainer venture. - **Sell now and Undercut now**: lists and vendors only what you picked, or only checks and undercuts your listings, visiting only the retainers that need it. - **Guarded pricing**: Undercut or Match against the same quality only, bait listings ignored, floors never below vendor value, and a step limit, cooldown and price-war detection against a race to the bottom. - **Never against yourself**: your own retainers and your alts are never undercut. - **Rules**: per-item floors, ceilings, fixed prices, lot sizes, keep counts and preferred retainers, category rules with a junk rule, and Never sell for anything protected. - **Sources**: your bags and crystals, and when you opt in, a retainer's own inventory, the saddlebag and the armoury chest. - **Assist**: compares prices when you open a sell window by hand and fills the suggested price, leaving Confirm to you. - **In-game buttons**: Run all retainers on the retainer list, Reprice this retainer on a sell list, and Sell now on AutoRetainer's list. - **Undercut watch**: your listings checked against Universalis on a timer, with no game request. - **Sales**: a ledger of every sale with daily, 7-day and 30-day totals, a chart, hints on what sells fast or sits unsold, and a CSV export. - **Run controls**: Pause, Resume and Stop, auto-pause while you're in a duty, and hold new moves while you type in chat. - **Humanizer**: short random delays before moving off or teleporting. - **GM alert**: ends a run when a GM is near, with optional toast, chat line, beeps, custom commands, or closing the game. - **Runs and console**: past runs with their outcome, and every step logged on the Console page, ready to copy into a bug report. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. The plugin needs **vnavmesh** to walk to a summoning bell, and uses **AutoRetainer** when it is installed to run after ventures, respect its protect list and know your alts. Open `/asell deps` after install to see the list and one-click each missing one. Runs work for the current character on its home world; for your first runs, sell one cheap item with low limits per run and watch the whole run. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/asell` | Toggle the main window | | `/seller` | Alias for `/asell` | | `/asell config` | Open the Settings page | | `/asell stats` | Open the Runs tab of the Sales page (`/asell history` works too) | | `/asell sales` | Open the Sales page | | `/asell deps` | Open the Plugins page (`/asell dependencies` works too) | | `/asell log` | Open the Console page | | `/asell changelog` | Open the Changelog page | | `/asell about` | Open the About page | | `/asell start` | Start a run of the current plan | | `/asell stop` | Stop the current run | | `/asell pause` | Pause or resume the current run (`/asell resume` works too) | | `/asell help` | List these commands in the chat | | `/asell target` | Log targeted NPC's BaseId (debug helper) | | `/asell look ` | Compare market prices for one item once and write them to the Console; never lists or reprices (debug helper) | | `/asell mbstatus` | Write the market checks, the search state and the age of the Universalis reference data to the Console (debug helper) | | `/asell sendpath compare\|proxy` | Choose how `/asell look` sends its searches; alone, shows which one is in use (debug helper) | | `/asell historypath window\|packet` | Choose where a retainer's sale history is read from; alone, shows which one is in use (debug helper) | ## Languages The windows are available in English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, 日本語, and 中文. website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto PVP LB

Your PvP Limit Break, fired for you. Built on Dalamud.

---

## What it does Monitors enemy HP during PvP. When the target's HP drops below your configured threshold, fires your job's PvP Limit Break. Great for burst jobs like Ninja or Machinist to lock in kills. Jobs whose PvP LB is defensive or support-focused (e.g. Paladin's Phalanx) are flagged in the status window and never auto-fired. ## Features - **Configurable threshold**: percent of max HP or absolute HP, with per-job overrides. - **Range- and shape-aware targeting**: single-target LBs respect cast range; circle-around-target LBs prefer clustered enemies; PBAoE LBs fire when any below-threshold enemy is in radius. - **Shield-aware HP**: threshold checks against effective HP (`CurrentHp + ShieldHp`) so shields don't trigger early fires. - **Skip doomed targets**: predicts time-to-death and skips enemies that will die before the LB lands. - **Player blocklist + duty filter**: named players are never targeted; per-mode checkboxes (CC / Frontline / Rival Wings / Custom Match / Other) scope auto-fire. - **Auto-target**: picks the lowest-effective-HP hostile in range; falls back to manual hard target when off. - **Status window**: current target, HP bar with shield overlay and threshold marker, distance, range/shape, granular readiness (`READY` / `FIRING` / `PAUSED` / `OUT OF RANGE` / `GAUGE LOW` / `DEFENSIVE`). - **Session + lifetime stats**: fires, attributed kills, total enemies hit. Lifetime persists across reloads. - **Optional feedback**: chat sound (`/se1`–`/se16`) and/or chat line on fire. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Auto PVP LB**, and install. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/pvpautolb` | Toggle the status window | | `/palb` | Alias for `/pvpautolb` | | `/pvpautolb config` | Open settings | ## Configuration Open via `/pvpautolb config` or the gear icon in the status window. - **Threshold**: mode (percent / absolute) and value. Below this, the LB fires. - **Per-job override**: each job can have its own threshold mode and value. - **Targeting**: auto-select toggle and scan radius (5–50 yalms). When off, only your hard target is considered. - **Filters**: skip doomed targets, allowed duty types (CC / Frontline / Rival Wings / Custom / Other). - **Player blocklist**: names listed here are never auto-targeted. - **Feedback**: optional chat sound and/or chat line on fire. ## Job compatibility Limit Breaks are resolved from game data, so every job is wired up automatically. The table tracks what has been verified in live PvP matches. If you test a job, please open an issue or PR. **Legend:** ✅ confirmed · ❔ untested · 🛡 defensive/support: not auto-fired | Tanks | Status | | Healers | Status | |---|---|---|---|---| | Paladin | 🛡 Phalanx | | White Mage | ✅ | | Warrior | 🛡 Primal Scream | | Scholar | 🛡 Seraphism | | Dark Knight | ✅ | | Astrologian | 🛡 Celestial River | | Gunbreaker | ✅ | | Sage | 🛡 Mesotes | | Melee DPS | Status | | Ranged DPS | Status | |---|---|---|---|---| | Monk | ✅ | | Bard | 🛡 Final Fantasia | | Dragoon | ✅ | | Machinist | ✅ | | Ninja | ✅ | | Dancer | 🛡 Contradance | | Samurai | ✅ | | Black Mage | 🛡 Soul Resonance | | Reaper | 🛡 Tenebrae Lemurum | | Summoner | 🛡 Phoenix & Bahamut | | Viper | ✅ | | Red Mage | ✅ Southern Cross | | | | | Pictomancer | 🛡 Advent of Chocobastion | ## More from me If you liked this plugin, take a look at my other Dalamud work. website.description: Doman Mahjong, solved for you.
website.readmeExcerpt:
# Auto Mahjong Solver

A Dalamud plugin that reads FFXIV Doman Mahjong, computes the mathematically best discard and call, shows a suggestion overlay, and (optionally, behind a gate) plays for you.

Command: `/amjs` (alias `/mahjong`).

## Status

The solver engine, board reading, and the autonomous play loop are live-verified on casual tables
(multi-hand sessions without stalls). Riichi declaration and the defense layer are implemented and
await their first observed in-game trigger.

| Capability | State |
|---|---|
| Solver engine (shanten, ukeire) | Implemented, unit-tested |
| Yaku / Doman scoring | Implemented, unit-tested; han→points table pending live verification |
| `Emj` hand reader (closed hand, aka) | **Verified live** (incl. under popups) |
| `Emj` meld reader (chii/pon/kan, feeds meldCount) | **Verified live** — meld strips mapped (self=112 family); post-call discard state 28 handled |
| `Emj` addon reader (rivers, dora, winds, scores, riichi badges) | Implemented; opponent river↔panel pairing pending live verification (`/amjs state`) |
| Seen-tile ukeire + furiten avoidance + fold vs riichi | Implemented; fold path awaits first observed opponent riichi |
| Auto-riichi (declare on live closed tenpai, then tsumogiri) | **Verified live** |
| Auto-play loop (discard, win, calls, redeal prompt, result screens) | **Verified live** — multi-hand sessions; popup fires retry-verified; settle grace + stall watchdog |
| Nine-terminals redeal prompt (keep on kokushi shanten ≤ 2) | Implemented; option label match pending first observation |
| Value-aware discard EV (exact points EV at tenpai; dora/aka/yakuhai retention above) | Implemented, unit-tested |
| Shared turn policy (engine `TurnPolicy`, used by bot and simulator) | Implemented |
| Self-play simulator (`tools/AutoMahjongSolver.Simulator`) | Implemented; baseline below |
| Calling strategy v1 (pon: yakuhai / secured-yaku / dora-tanyao; chi+kan never) | Implemented, unit-tested, simulated; pending live verification |
| Suggestion overlay | Planned |
| Chi / kan calls | Planned (chi variant-selection UI unverified; kan flips unreadable dora) |

## Layout

- `AutoMahjongSolver.Engine` — pure C# (`net10.0`), no Dalamud dependency. Tiles, shanten, ukeire, and (later) yaku/scoring. Fully unit-testable offline.
- `tests/AutoMahjongSolver.Engine.Tests` — xUnit tests for the engine.
- `AutoMahjongSolver` — the Dalamud plugin (planned): `Emj` reader, suggestion overlay, gated actuation. Built on ECommons.

## Build

```
dotnet test                                                   # engine + tests (no game required)
dotnet run --project tools/AutoMahjongSolver.Simulator -c Release -- 200 7   # self-play: matches, seed
```

Self-play baseline (200 matches, seed 7, all four seats on the current policy), with pon calls
(2026-06-12): 1125 hands, ~17.5% win rate per seat-hand, ~9.7% deal-in, ~30.5% riichi, 30.1%
exhaustive draws, average win 5990 points / 3.31 han. The closed-hands-only run before calls was
38.7% draws / 15.3% wins / 7.2% deal-in / avg win 7302 — pon trades win size for completion rate.
Policy changes should be judged against these numbers, same seed.

The Dalamud plugin project builds against `Dalamud.NET.Sdk` and requires a Dalamud dev environment.

## Notes

Doman Mahjong is standard 4-player Japanese riichi with FFXIV-specific scoring: a flat han-to-points table with **no fu calculation**. The engine targets this ruleset.

Auto-play of a ranked, human-PvP minigame carries account risk. Auto-play is off by default, gated behind an explicit opt-in, and disabled in ranked rooms.

## What it is Aetherphone is the first and only fully working phone plugin for FINAL FANTASY XIV: a docked, always-on device with a home screen, an app switcher, and notifications. Behind the apps runs its own social network, so what you post, send, and save carries across characters, worlds, and sessions instead of living only on your machine. ## Highlights - **A phone that lives in your HUD.** Drag it anywhere, size it how you like, and minimize it into a mini phone that shows only the widgets you pick and resizes from its corner just like the full phone. It can also fold into a live zone minimap and take the game minimap's place. - **Message anyone, on any world.** ChocoChat reaches every Aetherphone user no matter their world or data center, with voice notes, group chats, and voice calls you place straight from a contact. No party, no friend list, no travel. - **Social apps of your own.** Chirper for short posts, Aethergram for photos, and Velvet, an optional 18+ companion. One identity carries across all of them and follows you between characters. - **Every game chat channel, reorganized.** Linkpearl puts all of game chat in tabs you build yourself, with tells as their own conversations, per-channel colors, and a composer that splits and paces messages the game would cut off. Read each tab as a log or as chat bubbles, pick a chat theme and wallpaper, import the game's channel colors, and mask names for screenshots. - **Chat with the phone closed.** Pop any conversation into a floating window that lands beside the phone, let new chats join it as tabs, and let it hide during combat and duties, then come back on its own. - **Apps that play the game with you.** Strats for raid cheatsheets with your spot marked on each mechanic, Hunts for marks and trains, Fishing for ocean voyages, plus Market, Housing, Maps, Venues, Dailies, Collections, and Inventory. - **The everyday utilities too.** Notes, Calendar, Timers for resets and retainers, Calculator, Wallet, Camera and Photos with your own albums and a built-in photo editor, Clock, Skywatcher for weather, and Shortcuts you can fire from a hotbar macro. - **Watch and listen together.** MogCast casts video onto an in-world screen with playback synced for everyone present, and Music brings live community radio and Rolladeck DJ sets in game. - **Speaks your language.** One-tap translation on posts, profiles, and private messages, with feeds and chats able to translate everything as it arrives. - **Downtime built in.** Gamba is a play-money casino with blackjack, slots, scratch cards, bingo, and a communal wheel, and nothing there has cash value. Games is an arcade of thirty-plus titles with Doom among them, plus Uno, Chess, and Pool against friends online. - **Make it yours.** Custom wallpapers, your own ringtone and notification sounds, any accent color, Lodestone character portraits, subtle interface sounds, and a text-size zoom. - **Private by design.** Messages, attachments, and voice notes are end-to-end encrypted, calls are encrypted in transit, and a human moderation team reviews public posts and images. Forty-two apps in all. Full feature tour, screenshots, and details live on the website: → **[www.aetherphone.net](https://www.aetherphone.net/)** ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Aetherphone**, and install. Playing the Chinese game version? The phone detects it, signs you in through your Rising Stones (石之家) profile instead of the Lodestone, and points the apps that need them at the Chinese worlds and news feed. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/phone` | Toggle the phone | | `/aetherphone` | Alias for `/phone` | | `/phone run ` | Run a shortcut by name, so it can sit on a hotbar macro | | `/phone market [item]` | Open the market board, searching for an item if you name one | | `/phone reset` | Recenter the phone on screen | | `/phone test` | Send a sample notification | ## Community Questions, ideas, or just want to hang out with other players? website.readmeExcerpt:
Auto Hunt Grinder

Hunt bills, cleared for you. Built on Dalamud.

--- ## What it does Lists every daily and weekly hunt bill from A Realm Reborn through Dawntrail in one window. Tick the bills you want and press **Start**: the plugin travels to each hunt board you still need a bill from, accepts it, then teleports and flies to every mark on your bills, fights it, and moves on until each bill is done. ## Features - **Every hunt board**: Grand Company, clan and guildship bills from ARR through DT, dailies and weekly Elite Marks, with boards you haven't unlocked yet greyed out. - **Live bill progress**: reads the bills you hold and your kill counts straight from the game, so the window always matches what the game shows. - **Board pickup**: walks up to the hunt board and accepts any selected bill you aren't holding yet, and finishes an older bill before it takes the new one. - **Route planning**: groups marks by zone, so a run teleports as little as possible. - **Mark finder**: flies to each mark's known spawn points and sweeps them until it shows up, and patrols elite marks for a while before moving on. - **Hands-off combat**: fights each mark with a bundled combat preset that never pulls other mobs, and only counts a kill once the bill does. - **Recovery**: gets back up after a death and tries the mark again a few times; re-paths, jumps, or teleports out when it gets stuck. - **After-run action**: stay logged in, log out, or close the game once every bill is done. - **Auto-repair**: Dark Matter first, Grand Company mender as fallback. - **Auto-consume**: keeps food and medicine buffs up between marks, HQ first. - **Humanizer**: takes random city breaks between marks so long sessions look less mechanical. - **Pause & resume**: park a run without losing your progress, and auto-pause while you're in a duty. - **Party invites**: auto-declines incoming invites during a run after a random delay, with an optional reply message. - **GM alert**: stops the bot when a GM is near, with optional toast, beeps, or custom commands. - **History**: every run recorded with bills cleared, marks hunted, and seals or nuts earned. ## Install In-game: `/xlsettings` → **Experimental** → paste into **Custom Plugin Repositories**: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeldarAlz/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json ``` Tick **Enabled**, click **+**, then **Save and Close**. Open `/xlplugins` → **All Plugins**, search for **Auto Hunt Grinder**, and install. The plugin needs a few helpers for movement and combat to be installed and loaded. Open `/ahg deps` after install to see the list and one-click each missing one. ## Commands | Command | Action | |---|---| | `/ahg` | Toggle the main window | | `/huntgrinder` | Alias for `/ahg` | | `/ahg config` | Open the Settings page | | `/ahg stats` | Open the History page | | `/ahg deps` | Open the Plugins page | | `/ahg about` | Open the About page | | `/ahg pause` | Pause or resume the current run | | `/ahg target` | Log targeted NPC's BaseId (debug helper) | | `/ahg goto ` | Travel to a point, `/ahg goto stop` cancels (debug helper) | ## Languages The windows are available in English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, 日本語, and 中文.
